title: Good Leaders Explain the Logic Behind Their Everyday Beliefs
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article introduces "Belief-Because" statements, a concept from Brian Gottlieb's book Beyond the Hammer, in which leaders pair a stated belief with a specific evidence-based rationale ("We should pause the project because the risk assessment now shows a high probability of failure"). The piece argues that revealing the logic behind assertions reduces others' self-doubt, builds conviction, and makes proposals easier for others to adopt and repeat as their own. It frames this as a simple, learnable communication habit rather than a natural talent, and closes by urging leaders to be more intentional about grounding everyday statements in explicit reasons.
points: "Belief-Because" statements, a concept from Brian Gottlieb's Beyond the Hammer, pair a belief with a specific evidence-based rationale.
Providing the logic behind a proposal reduces others' self-doubt and builds conviction they can adopt as their own.
People tend to repeat the rationale a leader offers, which makes proposals easier to accept and spread.
This is framed as a learnable habit — being intentional about grounding everyday beliefs and proposals in explicit reasons.
quotes: you will frequently hear them use simple statements that justify their beliefs with evidence, facts, and data.
Brian Gottlieb, former CEO and the author of Beyond the Hammer , calls these expressions Belief-Because statements .
These evidence-based affirmations pair a core belief with a specific “because” rationale.
Belief-Because statements combat self-doubt by providing logical anchors for others to grab onto and adopt.
Give people a short and simple rationale for your beliefs and convictions. They will hop on board faster that way.
